Everything is under /home/mherwig/.cache/research-lang/dotnet-tools/fixtures/heldout1-csasynclang/ (stage.sh, runcells.sh, out/). Held-out clones are untouched.

Staging: per tree, src is the production projects and tests the test projects, copied from the full clone. Mapping: nj=Src/Newtonsoft.Json, moq=src/Moq*, bogus=Source/Bogus, scriban=src/Scriban, mailkit=MailKit, dt=src/{ImageBuilder*,GitAutomation*,Infrastructure}.

No tree needed a different SDK. Their global.json files resolved: dt asks for 11.0.100-preview.5 with rollForward latestMajor, bogus for 10.0.100 with latestFeature. Skills and rules did not mishandle either. I did not run `G` (the full build gate): no tree has the posture files installed, so it would not test the rules.

Result: no genuinely new mechanism. Every failure maps to a known class. Contradiction between owning rows, dead or false-negative pattern, unenforced gap, broken step and redundant row each recur. The Redundant-row class (rule noisy or wrong on real trees) accounts for about half the failures, and I tagged those known=true. If the orchestrator wants it split, the sub-pattern is "MUST rule has no exemption for real, well-run code" (see findings 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16). No failure proposes a new MUST.

Cells that behaved correctly (hits read, true positives):
- C07: MailKit's 7 `new TaskCompletionSource<bool> ()` are real violations.
- C21b: no hits on any tree.
- C25a: dt's `new SemaphoreSlim(1)` x4 are real.

Adopter-only cells (C19a, L03a, L05a, L08, L21a, L22a, L24a/b) print violations or nothing on any non-adopter. That is by design, not a failure.

failures.problem: CS-LANG-05 says never write `new ArgumentNullException(`. CS-LANG-19 says 'after `_x = x ?? throw ...` read `_x`'. `ThrowIfNull` returns void, so a primary-constructor field initializer or ctor assignment has no single-expression guard other than `x ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(x))`. L05b flags exactly that idiom.
failures.evidence: L05b hits: dt 71 of 71 contain `?? throw` (63 are `_f = x ?? throw`, e.g. AzureDevOpsPullRequestEndpoint.cs:22 `private readonly AzureDevOpsClient _client = client ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(client));`). moq 7 of 20, scriban 14 of 100.
failures.fix: Allow `?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(x))` as the single-expression form for field initializers and primary-constructor parameters, and exclude `\?\?\s*throw` from L05b. Or keep the ban and name the replacement for primary constructors, and drop the `?? throw` example from CS-LANG-19.

failures.problem: Many patterns write `\(` with no `\s*` before the paren, so code styled `Method (args)` is invisible. MailKit and MimeKit use that style throughout.

They are absent from C12 (10 hits, all finalizers or SuppressFinalize), although an independent `Dispose\s*\(\s*bool` finds 15 lines. Only C07, C12 finalizer and SuppressFinalize, and C21a `Lazy<` fired.
failures.fix: Replace `\(` with `\s*\(` after every method or type name in C06, C09a, C09b, C11, C12 (`Dispose\s*\(`), C17, C21a, C22, C23a, C25a and C29, and add a spaced-style plant to the variants file the cells are watched against.

failures.problem: CS-ASYNC-08 mandates a per-attempt local `new CancellationTokenSource(timeout)` linked with the caller token. C20 greps every `CancellationTokenSource` line in any `*Client*.cs` file, though CS-ASYNC-20 forbids only fields. A client that implements its own timeouts is flagged for following ASYNC-08.

report:
SCOPE. 56 verification cells extracted from rules/csharp-quality/processes.md (CS-PROC rows, blocks P1..P8) and binaries.md (CS-BIN greps, jq pin gate, triangulate.py, canary block) and run verbatim over all 6 round trees (56 cells x 6 trees = 336 runs; the jq gate and triangulate.py ran on synthetic inputs because no tree has a pin file; the canary block is an adopter-built project and was not run). SECOND-WAY GREPS. Process subject (Process.Start, ProcessStartInfo, new Process, Kill, WaitForExit, Begin*ReadLine, Redirect*, ArgumentList, .Arguments=): only docker-tools. It has string argv everywhere (new ProcessStartInfo(fileName, args), `processStartInfo.Arguments = string.Join(' ', dockerArgs)`), event-mode reads plus sync WaitForExit, bare Kill() in TryKillProcess, ct.Register-based kill, uncapped StringBuilder capture, no CreateNoWindow anywhere, stdin redirected in 1 of 3 launches, secrets in argv through BuildSecretMode.BuildArgs. Compiled under the shipped ban file, the real ExecuteHelper.cs and ProcessRunner.cs raised RS0030 on ProcessStartInfo(String,String) x2, ProcessStartInfo.Arguments x2, BeginOutputReadLine, BeginErrorReadLine, WaitForExit(), Kill(), ReadToEndAsync x2 (net10.0), so the bans do fire on real code; no ban fires on the event subscription itself, which is inert. Encoding.UTF8 / GetString(byte[],int,int) usage: 83 sites across the 6 trees (MailKit 62+14), every one a GetBytes/GetString/GetChars call that cannot emit a BOM, zero StreamWriter(..., Encoding.UTF8) sites. HttpClient: docker-tools mixes AddHttpClient/IHttpClientFactory with one `new HttpClient(handler)`. Hash comparison, archive extraction, TLS callbacks `=> true`, signal handlers, shell-outs (sh/cmd/-c/.cmd/.bat): no instance outside tests in any tree.

PLANTS (cells run on _plant): confirmed false negatives for PROC-02a/03 (target-typed `new()` and `new Process{StartInfo}.Start()`), PROC-15a (`catch (TaskCanceledException)` unmatched; `when` on the next line is a false positive), PROC-15b (`callerToken` false positive, `linked.Token` false negative), PROC-22b (`TimeProvider`, `_clock`, multi-line argument all false positives), BIN-07 (`string.Equals(Convert.ToHexString(h), e, ...)` and `.Equals(` silent), BIN-08 (`(?i)^..$`, `"^" + x + "$"`, `@"^[^""]+$"`, unanchored-start `...{64}$` silent), BIN-11 (GetFromJsonAsync, GetAsync default buffering, GetStreamAsync not in grep or ban file). jq pin gate: genuine rc 0; trailing newline, 63-char, empty pins, uppercase, numeric version all rc 1 (correct). triangulate.py: genuine rc 0; one missing sha256.sum row rc 0 with `DIFF`/mismatches 1 (correct nonzero path in script, it exits 1 on bad); a version absent from the manifest prints `rows 0 mismatches 0` and exits 0.

RULE-VS-REAL-CODE. (1) PROC-11's repo-wide Encoding.UTF8 / GetString ban turns ~83 correct sites red for a hazard (BOM on a pipe writer) that occurs in none of the trees. (2) PROC-12 "no newline" is the reference tool's contract stated universally; docker login --password-stdin and git/credential line protocols need or tolerate a terminator. (3) BIN-14 prescribes one static readonly HttpClient and omits IHttpClientFactory, which the research corpus (failure.md) names as the other accepted fix and which the best-run tree here uses. (4) BIN-16 offers only CustomRootTrust; a TLS client library with a documented user hook (MailKit) must install a RemoteCertificateValidationCallback, and its default is strict. (5) MailKit targets netstandard2.0/net462 which these rows do not cover (rows bind to net8.0/net10.0), so BIN-16 and PROC-11 are partly out of the stated TFM scope there. (6) PROC-09's ReadToEndAsync ban is justified in PROC-10/13 (cap, post-exit EOF stall); GitAutomation's concurrent-start ReadToEndAsync form does not deadlock, so the PROC-09 rationale alone does not explain the ban; low.

NEW VS KNOWN. Almost everything maps to existing classes (Dead or false-negative pattern, Unenforced claim/gap, Contradiction, Redundant row/noise). Two items match no class: PROC-12 (tool-specific mechanism stated as a universal MUST) and BIN-14 (rule omits the framework-idiomatic alternative that the research corpus names). report:
PHASE 8 HELD-OUT ROUND 1: rules/csharp-quality/security.md and observability.md

SCOPE
Ran every verification cell of both files over all 6 trees (grep blocks, gate/pack/build-code/registry blocks, the nuspec greps, the licences script, the RS0030 ban set). That is roughly 270 cell-runs. Work area: /home/mherwig/.cache/research-lang/dotnet-tools/fixtures/heldout1-secobs/ (copies, with per-cell outputs in _work/out/<tree>/). The held-out clones were not modified.

HOW I RAN THEM
- The cells are verbatim, with `src` and `tests` replaced by each tree's real production and test directories.
- I also ran the verbatim `src` form where a `src` directory exists. Run that way, the Moq `Guid.NewGuid()` grep returns 7 hits, all in tests, against 0 in production code.
- I proved my harness on planted files before trusting zero-hit results.
- Builds (SDK 10.0.401, via run.sh):
  - `dotnet pack` for Newtonsoft.Json, Bogus and Scriban. MailKit failed because its submodule is absent. Moq produced no nupkg.
  - The CS-SEC-01 gate evaluated on every csproj in all 6 trees.
  - A posture build (the real BannedSymbols.txt, BannedSymbols.Src.txt and analyzers.globalconfig, with `AnalysisLevel=10.0-all`) on Bogus, Scriban and Newtonsoft.Json.
- Scriban needed central package management for the posture build. That is a harness detail, not a rule fault.

WHAT THE TREES SHOW
- The JSON, wrapper and CLI shape of the reference consumer holds for none of these trees. Only docker-tools uses MEL, with 126 `ILogger` mentions, 291 extension `LogX` calls and 0 `[LoggerMessage]`. So the observability grep rows are mostly vacuous (0 hits) here.
- Security: the posture build confirms RS0030 fires on real code. Newtonsoft: `Type.GetType`, `Assembly.GetType`, `Trace`. Bogus: literal `new Regex(@"...")`. This is the safety net behind the grep false negatives.
- Measured under the posture: Scriban gets CA5350 as error (the `sha1` and `hmac_sha1` template functions) and CA5351 and CA5394 as warnings. Bogus gets CA5394 ×8. Newtonsoft gets CA2326 ×7.
- Per-tree summary of the failing cells:
  - Newtonsoft.Json: SEC-03 default `Regex.InfiniteMatchTimeout`, SEC-04 61 hits that are its own TypeNameHandling feature, SEC-05 35 hits that are its XML converter.
  - MailKit: SEC-08 MD5/SHA1 (12 hits), SEC-06 `SYSLIB0011` NoWarn in UnitTests, OBS-17 and OBS-22 multi-protocol telemetry (4 meters, 5 instruments), OBS-21 `ActivityStatusCode.Ok`.
  - Bogus: SEC-07 `new Random(seed)` by design, SEC-06 `EnableUnsafeBinaryFormatterSerialization` in the NUKE Builder project.
  - Scriban: SEC-07 `new Random()` for the template `random` function, SEC-08 md5/sha1, SEC-03 default timeout 10 s.
  - docker-tools: OBS-02 291 extension calls, OBS-12 5 working `Verify(l => l.Log(...))` mocks, OBS-07 2 log-and-rethrow sites.
  - Moq: no real rule violations. Its hits are all false positives (resx files, an `IMock<ILogger>` inside a code string).

FAILURES BY CLASS (full rows in the structured list)

1. NEW class: scope overreach. A universal MUST, verified by an unconditional cell, is derived from one reference consumer (a JSON CLI wrapper). Real well-run code of another shape violates it for a product or protocol reason, and no carve-out exists.
   - SEC-01/06/08 (weak hash). The rationale "No protocol the library speaks mandates a weak hash" is false. MailKit speaks CRAM-MD5, DIGEST-MD5, SCRAM-SHA-1, NTLM and POP3 APOP. Scriban ships md5, sha1 and hmac_sha1 as template functions. Under the posture CA5350 is an error, and no suppression is allowed, so the rule cannot be met.
   - SEC-07 (`RandomNumberGenerator` only). Bogus is seeded and deterministic by product design.
   - SEC-04/05. Newtonsoft implements the feature the rule bans.
   - OBS-16. Newtonsoft's `DiagnosticsTraceWriter` is a Trace-backed feature, and RS0030 fires on `Trace`.
   - OBS-02, OBS-07, OBS-12. docker-tools is a Microsoft CLI app, and a MUST against the whole app is high friction.
   - OBS-17/20/21/22. These conflict with MailKit's multi-protocol, opt-in telemetry.

2. Known class "Dead or false-negative pattern".
   - Space-before-paren style (`AddTag ("server.address"`, `StartActivity (`). MailKit uses it everywhere. OBS-19, OBS-20 (including the allow-list diff, which prints empty while the code records 4 tag keys) and OBS-02 all miss it.
   - OBS-09 and OBS-19 lack `-U`, so they miss multi-line forms (planted).
   - The SEC-04 grep omits `Type.GetType` and `Assembly.Load`. Newtonsoft has 8 and 7 of them; only the ban catches them.
   - The SEC-03 grep skips literal patterns. Bogus has about 8.
   - The SEC-09 cell passes vacuously when the nuspec has no net10.0 group (Bogus, Scriban).
   - The SEC-01 gate flags equivalent spellings `AnalysisLevel=latest-all` and `AnalysisMode=All` (probed).

3. Known class "Broken step or placeholder".
   - Three of the 6 trees have no `src`: Newtonsoft uses `Src`, Bogus `Source`, MailKit `MailKit`. Run verbatim, `rg` writes an error to stderr and exits 2 with empty stdout, which the file's "empty output passes" wording reads as a pass.
   - Three trees keep production and tests under one `src`.
   - `Directory.Packages.props` is hardcoded at the repo root, but the 3 CPM trees (Scriban, Moq, docker-tools) keep it in `src/`. Moq's `nuget.config` is also in `src/`.
   - The CS-SEC-11 analyzers cell hardcodes `-p:TargetFramework=net10.0`. Scriban targets netstandard2.0;net8.0, so it gets NETSDK1005 and a jq parse error.
   - The CS-SEC-12 existence check uses the NuGet search API, so it returns false NOT-FOUND for real packages:
     - PolySharp (version 1.16.0+sha, needs `semVerLevel=2.0.0`).
     - Stunts, Stunts.CodeAnalysis, Stunts.DynamicProxy, Stunts.StaticProxy and ManualStunts (dotted prerelease versions).
     - Microsoft.DotNet.VersionTools (private dnceng feed).
     - The flat container returns 200 for polysharp and stunts and 404 for the fake IDs. The rule says NOT-FOUND blocks the change.
   - The CS-SEC-08 `rg -l FixedTimeEquals | wc -l` "must print 1" cell prints 0 on all 6 trees, because none authenticates a download. OBS-22 "must print 1" prints 0 on 5 of 6 non-emitting trees.

4. Known class "Redundant row or script" (cell noise).
   - SEC-03 review aid. The second command flags correct four-argument calls: Scriban 5/5, and Newtonsoft `QueryExpression.cs:239`.
   - SEC-03 first command hits a doc cref in Scriban.
   - SEC-05 has no `*.cs` glob, so it hits .resx (Moq ×3), .yml and .csproj. It also hits `System.Data.SqlTypes` (Newtonsoft) and an unused `using System.Data;` (Scriban).
   - SEC-06 second command scans `.`. It hits the NUKE build project in Bogus, which is outside `src`.
   - SEC-08 `SequenceEqual` hits are 4/4 non-authentication.
   - OBS-06 `{Error}` matches a string placeholder, not an exception.
   - OBS-07 has 13 false positives out of 17 non-docker hits (Scriban 12, Moq 1).
   - OBS-12 has 1 false positive in Moq.
   - OBS-15 hits an app composition root in docker-tools.
   - OBS-20a matches `KeyValuePair<string, object?>` dictionary entries in Scriban.
   - SEC-11 and SEC-13 list SDK-implicit packages (netstandard.library, ILLink, the reference assemblies) as build code or NO-SPDX-EXPRESSION. That is about 50% of Newtonsoft's closure (7 of 14 packages) and 12+ of Bogus's 72.

5. Passes. These cells work as written on real trees: the CS-SEC-14 awk (it handles Moq's zero-indent entries), SEC-10 (both commands), the SEC-11 triage greps, the nuspec greps, `posture-check`-style `uniq -d`, and the RS0030 ban set.
   - Expected failures, not defects: no tree has a Dependabot cooldown (CS-SEC-14), and none has the posture installed.

NO NEW MUST PROPOSED
Every finding is a correction to an existing row or cell. The one open question for the opus pass is whether "scope overreach" is a new class or an instance of "Unfaithful claim". I marked it new because the claim is a design assumption, not a mis-measurement.

Mail and auth protocols, and feature hashes such as template md5/sha1/hmac_sha1, mandate or ship exactly those hashes. The rule is unsatisfiable without deleting the product feature. new_classes.mechanism: A rule written and verified against the reference consumer (greenfield net8/net10 library wrapping a CLI, System.Text.Json, MTP, GitHub Actions) binds every repo its glob loads in with no applicability statement; on an app, a VSTest repo, a legacy-TFM library or a serializer library it demands what does not apply. Phase 8 reviewed only against the reference consumer, so it could not surface this. 12 instances (PROC-12, LANG-18, legacy TFMs in PERF/XP/TEST, PERF-09 benchmarks, TEST-08/09/10/27, SEC-04/05, OBS-02/07/12, BUILD/PKG misfit, analyzer-posture adoption, MTP-only index rules, Non-Negotiables, upgrade sibling Exe projects).
new_classes.check: For each MUST and Non-Negotiable, write its applicability (always, stj, cli-wrapper, packable-library, mtp, gha, greenfield). Run its cell on one held-out tree outside that applicability: every hit there must be silenced by the tag or be a real defect.

new_classes.name: No sanctioned form for a legitimate use
new_classes.mechanism: A MUST or ban has no exception route, yet well-run code inside its scope breaks it deliberately for a reason the row never names: protocol-mandated MD5/SHA1, a seeded RNG that is the product, protected virtual Dispose(bool) on an abstract public base, `is null` in an expression tree (CS8122), continue-on-error plus an outcome gate step, committed generator output, a #nullable disable migration, an isolating Directory.Build.props, a user-supplied regex with a timeout, IHttpClientFactory. 20 instances.
new_classes.check: For every MUST hit on a held-out well-run tree, read the site. If the maintainer did it on purpose (comment, design, compile constraint), the row must name the sanctioned form and its cell must pass that form.

new_classes.name: Organic failure outside a plant-built catalogue
new_classes.mechanism: dotnet-diagnose rows came from planted breakage. Host- or checkout-origin failures (OpenSSL SHA1 policy breaking strong-name signing, SourceLink on repositoryformatversion=1, uninitialised submodule MSB3202, missing shared runtime, VSTest zero-match filter, transient MSB4018) have no row, and the step-3 fallback (Learn page for the code) is unusable on a code-less error. 6 instances.
new_classes.check: Run the triage capture verbatim on six fresh held-out clones in a stock environment (blob-less clone, distro crypto policy, default SDK set, submodules not initialised); route every failure. Each must land on a row or a fallback that names an action, code-less errors included.

new_classes.name: Unbounded side effect of a prescribed command
new_classes.mechanism: A block writes a large state directory (NUGET_PACKAGES=$(mktemp -d), --packages $(mktemp -d)) and never removes it; repeated runs fill a tmpfs (6.1 GB over five gate runs, ENOSPC), and the code-less NuGet error then hides behind the code-only log filter. 3 instances (index Gate, DN-UPG-04, DN-DIAG step 5).
new_classes.check: Run each fenced block twice with TMPDIR on a small quota directory and compare du before and after; any growth beyond the log needs a trap ... EXIT cleanup and a stated per-run size.
